blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At senior levels, networks of influence are less about contacts and more about trust accumulated over long periods. The executives whose phone calls actually get returned are rarely the most aggressive networkers; they are the people who, over a decade or more, have built a reputation for being reliable, discreet and generous with their own time when nothing was at stake.

That reputation, once established, is a genuine form of strategic capital. It moves decisions faster. It opens doors that stay closed to others, and it provides early signals about opportunities and risks that would otherwise remain invisible. Unlike most other forms of capital, however, it cannot be built quickly — and attempting to do so is usually painfully visible.

Networks also decay silently if neglected. The relationships that matter most tend to be maintained at a low, steady frequency — a short message here, a small introduction there — rather than revived in the week something is needed. Revival under pressure rarely works, and is easily spotted by the other side. Tend the garden when nothing is growing; the harvest takes care of itself.

items.q: According to the text, whose phone calls actually get returned at senior levels?
options: Executives who make the most requests
Those with the largest number of contacts
People with a long-standing reputation for reliability and discretion
The most aggressive networkers
items.why: "they are the people who, over a decade or more, have built a reputation for being reliable, discreet and generous."

items.q: What is said to happen to networks that are neglected?
options: They grow more valuable
They collapse loudly and visibly
They stay exactly as they were
They decay silently
items.why: "Networks also decay silently if neglected."

items.q: Why is strategic capital described as different from most other forms of capital?
options: It can be sold to competitors
It requires large financial investment
It is easy to measure precisely
It cannot be built quickly
items.why: "Unlike most other forms of capital, however, it cannot be built quickly."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Trust is accumulated over long periods.
A reputation for discretion is a strategic asset.
Reaching out only when you need something is an effective strategy.
Small, regular gestures keep relationships alive.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta que "revival under pressure rarely works, and is easily spotted" — o oportunismo de última hora é justamente o que ele condena.

items.q: What does "Tend the garden when nothing is growing" suggest?
options: You should invest in relationships precisely when you need nothing from them
Networking is a purely seasonal activity
Gardens are a poor metaphor for influence
Relationships should only be cultivated during a crisis
items.why: Inferência: a metáfora defende manter a relação no período em que nada está em jogo, para que ela esteja pronta quando a colheita chegar.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily conversando com um contato de longa data. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
It's genuinely good to see you — and no, before you ask, there's nothing on the agenda today. I didn't book this to sell you anything or to ask for a favour. Twelve years, and I think the last time we spoke I owed you an introduction, not the other way round.

I've come to believe that these are the conversations that actually matter. The ones where nothing is at stake. If I only ever picked up the phone the week I needed something, you'd see it coming a mile off — and honestly, you'd be right to.

So tell me how you're really doing. How's the new role treating you? And that project you mentioned last spring — did it ever find its feet?

Look, if there's anyone in my network who might be useful to you, say the word and I'll make the connection. No expectation attached. I've learned that the doors that open easiest are the ones you tended long before you ever needed them. Everything else takes care of itself.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why did Emily arrange this conversation?
options: To ask for a specific favour
For no particular agenda — simply to catch up
To sell the contact a product
To repay a business debt
items.why: "there's nothing on the agenda today. I didn't book this to sell you anything or to ask for a favour."

items.q: How long has Emily known this contact?
options: A decade and a half
Two years
Twelve months
Twelve years
items.why: "Twelve years, and I think the last time we spoke I owed you an introduction."

items.q: What does Emily offer the contact?
options: An introduction to someone useful, with no expectation attached
A share of a project's profits
Confidential information about a rival
A job in her own company
items.why: "if there's anyone in my network who might be useful to you… I'll make the connection. No expectation attached."

items.q: What does Emily imply with "you'd see it coming a mile off"?
options: The contact is unusually perceptive about everyone
Reaching out only when you need something is obvious and easily spotted
Long distances make relationships harder to maintain
She plans to call more often in future
items.why: Inferência: ela reconhece que o contato oportunista é transparente — o outro lado percebe na hora.

items.q: What underlying belief best captures Emily's approach to her network?
options: Influence is best built through frequent, high-pressure requests
Networking is only worthwhile when a deal is on the table
Business and personal contact should never mix
Relationships tended before they are needed are the ones that open doors
items.why: Inferência: "the doors that open easiest are the ones you tended long before you ever needed them" — a tese central da lição.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "A reputation for discretion is a genuine form of strategic capital." Strategic capital is…
options: money set aside for long-term investments
a formal line of credit from a bank
an intangible asset — such as trust or reputation — that confers lasting advantage
the number of employees a firm can deploy
items.why: Capital estratégico: um ativo intangível (confiança, reputação) que dá vantagem duradoura.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "She maintains her network at a low, steady ___, sending a short note here and a small introduction there."
options: frequency
hierarchy
deadline
expense
items.why: Low-frequency signal / low, steady frequency: manter a relação em ritmo baixo e constante.

items.q: "His quiet generosity — the introductions he made with no expectation — is why people trust him." Quiet generosity refers to…
options: an aggressive sales technique
large public donations announced in the press
helping others discreetly, without seeking anything in return
spending freely on client entertainment
items.why: Generosidade discreta: ajudar de forma silenciosa, sem cobrar retorno.

items.q: Discretion is best described as…
options: the habit of sharing news quickly
a formal reporting relationship
the freedom to make decisions without approval
the ability to keep matters confidential and act with tact
items.why: Discrição: saber guardar sigilo e agir com tato — descrita na lição como uma forma de generosidade.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Trust compounds on a ___, so the payoff of these relationships may not appear for years."
options: short fuse
tight budget
narrow margin
long horizon
items.why: Long horizon: horizonte longo — a confiança rende com o tempo, não de imediato.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem quando se fala de relacionamentos e influência. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "I try to keep in touch with people even when there's nothing on the table." To keep in touch means to…
options: meet only at formal events
monitor someone closely
maintain regular, ongoing contact
end a relationship politely
items.why: Keep in touch = manter contato regular ao longo do tempo.

items.q: "She'll put in a good word for you with the committee." To put in a good word means to…
options: recommend or speak favourably about someone
ask a direct question
correct someone's mistake tactfully
make a formal complaint
items.why: Put in a good word for = recomendar, falar bem de alguém para abrir portas.

items.q: "Don't reach out to contacts only when you need something." To reach out means to…
options: extend a deadline
avoid contact entirely
make contact or get in touch with someone
reject an offer
items.why: Reach out = entrar em contato, tomar a iniciativa de falar com alguém.

items.q: "He always follows up after a meeting with a short, thoughtful note." To follow up means to…
options: cancel the meeting afterwards
arrive late to the next meeting
delegate the work to someone else
take further action after an initial contact
items.why: Follow up = dar sequência, retomar após um primeiro contato.

items.q: "That old contact could open doors for us in the region." To open doors means to…
options: reveal confidential information
create opportunities or access that were otherwise closed
sign a formal contract
start an argument
items.why: Open doors = criar oportunidades e acessos que estariam fechados a outros.
